Rumor has it that Apple will release new products on October 13. Based on Apple's past October event timings, here's an estimate of when Apple might announce the event date.

Will Apple hold an October event?

Apple's September events have always been very regular, but the timing of its October events is hard to pin down — both the event date and the announcement lead time have been inconsistent.

Since 2010, Apple has held only 10 October events, the most recent being the Halloween-themed "Scary Fast" event on the evening of October 30, 2023.

Below is the lead time for each of Apple's October events since 2010:

Year Event Announcement date Event date 2023 “Scary Fast” Tuesday, October 24 Monday, October 30 2021 “Unleashed” Tuesday, October 12 Monday, October 18 2020 “Hi, Speed” Tuesday, October 6 Tuesday, October 13 2018 “There’s more in the making” Thursday, October 18 Tuesday, October 30 2016 “Hello again” Wednesday, October 19 Thursday, October 27 2014 “It’s been way too long” Wednesday, October 8 Thursday, October 16 2013 “We still have a lot to cover” Tuesday, October 15 Tuesday, October 22 2012 “We’ve got a little more to show you” Tuesday, October 16 Tuesday, October 23 2011 “Let’s talk iPhone” Tuesday, September 27 Tuesday, October 4 2010 “Back to the Mac” Wednesday, October 13 Wednesday, October 20

That said, Bloomberg recently reported that Apple plans to unveil the long-rumored smart home hub, the next-generation HomePod mini, and a new Apple TV 4K with the next-generation Siri AI features on Tuesday, October 13, but the report did not say whether Apple would hold an event to announce these products.

If true, Apple could announce the event date as early as next Monday (October 5), but no later than Wednesday, October 7.

It is worth noting that Apple is also expected to announce an iPad mini with an OLED display, a new iMac, and several new MacBook Pro models (including a touchscreen version) in 2026. Whether these products will appear at the same event, be announced at a separate event, or be released via press release remains unknown.

Looking back, Apple unveiled new Macs through press releases on three consecutive days in October 2024; similarly, in October 2025, Apple did not hold an event but directly announced the M5 chip along with new iPad Pro, MacBook Pro, and Apple Vision Pro.

By comparison, Apple has historically held only one event in November — back in November 2020, when the "One More Thing" event launched the first Macs powered by the M1 Apple Silicon chip.

Of course, 2020 was an unusual year for Apple's event schedule. In addition to the rare late-June WWDC, Apple also held separate events in September and October that year, all because the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted the normal timetable.

What new products do you think Apple will announce at the rumored October event? Let us know in the comments.
